What the official sources say

  • A landlord must return the security deposit or mail a written statement of exact reasons within 30 days after the lease ends or the premises are surrendered; a written lease may extend this up to 60 days (C.R.S. 38-12-103(1)). (Security Deposits, Judicial Legal Help Center (cites C.R.S. 38-12-103); source)
  • A landlord who wrongfully keeps a deposit may be liable for triple damages plus attorney fees and costs; tenant must give written notice of intent to sue at least 7 days before filing. (Security Deposits, Judicial Legal Help Center (C.R.S. 38-12-103); source)
  • HB25-1249 (effective Jan 1, 2026) requires a walk-through inspection on request, bars retaining deposit for preexisting damage, presumes bad faith if amount retained is 125% or more of actual damages, and requires transfer or return of a deposit within 60 days after the landlord's interest in the unit ends. (HB25-1249 Tenant Security Deposit Protections; source)
  • Warranty of habitability defense, C.R.S. 38-12-503: tenant must give written notice of the condition stating the landlord has five days to repair (unless tenant caused it). (Residential Evictions, Colorado Judicial Branch; source)

What rules does Colorado set for rental deposits?

Colorado caps a security deposit at two months of rent. That limit is in C.R.S. 38-12-102.5, as described in the Office of Legislative Legal Services renters' rights summary.

A few related limits sit next to it:

  • An extra pet deposit cannot be more than $300 and must be refundable.
  • A landlord may deduct for unpaid rent, abandonment, unpaid utilities and unpaid repair or cleaning the tenant agreed to pay. Normal wear and tear is not deductible.
  • A landlord who keeps any amount must send a written statement of the exact reasons and refund the rest. Missing the deadline forfeits the right to withhold anything.
  • A tenant cannot waive deposit rights, and a lease clause trying to do so is unenforceable.

The return deadline and the penalty for wrongful withholding already appear higher on this page, so we do not repeat them here.

What happens to a deposit when the landlord sells the house?

The deposit has to follow the change of ownership. Under C.R.S. 38-12-103(4), when a rental property changes hands, the deposit goes to the new owner or is returned to the tenant after lawful deductions.

The same rule applies to any change in ownership, including sale, assignment, death or receivership. An owner who sells a rented house therefore cannot simply keep the tenant's deposit and walk away.

That leaves two statutory paths at closing:

  1. Give the deposit to the buyer, and write the amount into the sale contract so both sides agree on it.
  2. Return it to the tenant, with the written itemization of any deductions, if the tenant is leaving.

Ask your title company how it wants the deposit shown on the settlement statement.

What is the warranty of habitability?

Every Colorado landlord warrants that a rental is fit to live in, and must keep it that way through the tenancy. The warranty sits in C.R.S. 38-12-503(1) and runs through the Part 5 statutes, which the legislature updated in 2024.

A breach has three parts: an uninhabitable condition, notice to the landlord, and a failure to begin or finish repairs. The statute sorts problems into two groups.

GroupExamples in the statute
Regular conditionsMold that materially affects health or safety, a substantial lack of working appliances, plumbing or gas not maintained, electrical systems not maintained, code violations
Conditions that materially interfere with life, health or safetyGas hazards, inadequate running or hot water, no electricity or hazardous wiring, no working exterior locks, rodent, pest or insect infestations

Tenants also have duties. They must keep the unit clean, safe and habitable, and a landlord is not responsible for problems the tenant caused through action, inaction or negligence.

How fast must a landlord respond to a repair notice?

For a condition that materially interferes with life, health or safety, remedial action must start within 24 hours of notice. That timing is in C.R.S. 38-12-503(2)(b), as summarized by the legislature's staff.

If the tenant asks, the landlord must also provide a comparable unit or a hotel room at no cost within 24 hours of the request. The landlord is presumed to have failed if such a condition persists seven calendar days after notice.

Work has to continue until the problem is fully fixed within a reasonable time. The landlord has a defense if the tenant caused the delay by denying entry, refusing a reasonable alternative time or otherwise slowing the repairs.

These timelines matter if you are thinking of selling a rental. Keep dated records of every repair notice and every response, since a buyer will ask for them.

What can a tenant do if repairs are not made?

The statute gives tenants several remedies, listed in C.R.S. 38-12-507.

  • Terminate the lease. If a condition is still unfixed after a reasonable time, the tenant can end the lease with 10 to 60 days of written notice, with a termination date at least 10 days out.
  • Terminate for a repeat problem. If the same condition returns within six months of being fixed, 10 days of written notice is enough.
  • Deduct repair costs from rent. This takes 10 days of written notice, or 48 hours for conditions that materially interfere with health or safety, plus a licensed or qualified professional and a chance for the landlord to fix it first.
  • Go to court. Actual and punitive damages, costs, reasonable attorney fees, injunctions, restraining orders and specific performance are all listed.

A landlord who plans to sell usually wants repairs done before showing the house, not after a tenant has started down one of these paths.

What counts as landlord retaliation?

Colorado bars a landlord from punishing a tenant for using habitability rights. Section 38-12-509 protects tenants who raise problems with the landlord, a third party or a government agency, or who join a tenants' organization.

Listed retaliatory acts include:

  • Raising rent or decreasing services.
  • Ending or declining to renew a lease without the tenant's written consent.
  • Starting or threatening an eviction.
  • Charging a fee, cost or penalty.
  • Intimidation, threats, discrimination or harassment.

A tenant who proves retaliation can recover damages, attorney fees and costs, and may end the lease. The tenant can also raise retaliation as a defense to a possession case. The statute does not stop a landlord from serving a notice to terminate or vacate where Colorado law allows one.

For a seller, timing is the lesson. A termination notice served right after a repair complaint invites a retaliation argument.

Does a landlord need a reason to end a Colorado tenancy?

Yes. Under House Bill 24-1098 and C.R.S. 38-12-1303, a landlord needs cause before serving a notice to terminate or filing a possession action. The legislature's summary lists 13 for-cause situations as of November 2024, including holding over after the lease ends, nonpayment, material lease violations and nuisance or negligent damage.

No-fault reasons are listed separately. One is that the landlord intends to stop renting and sell the home. The state's JDF 99 C form requires at least 90 days of notice for that route, with a move-out date after the lease term ends.

The form excludes tenants who have lived in the home less than a year, resident landlords of a single-family home, duplex or triplex, employer-provided housing, mobile home spaces and short-term rentals. The notice rules for how those cases proceed in court are covered on our eviction process page.

Whether a buyer takes the house with a tenancy in place depends on the sale contract, the lease and these notice rules.

How does this affect selling a rental house for cash?

A rental can be sold as is, with the tenant in place or after a lawful move-out. The law mostly decides how the tenancy ends, not whether the owner can sell.

Gather these items before talking to a buyer:

  • The lease and any amendments.
  • The deposit amount and where it is held.
  • Written repair requests and records of what was done.
  • Any notice already served and the date it was served.

With those in hand, a buyer can price the house and the closing can be built around the tenant's situation. We buy houses in Colorado as is, and we can walk through your lease and dates before you decide on a path. For legal questions, a Colorado attorney is the right call.

More questions about Colorado Landlord Tenant Law and Tenant Rights

How much can a Colorado landlord charge for a security deposit?

No more than two months of rent. An additional pet deposit is limited to $300 and must be refundable.

Can a landlord keep a deposit for normal wear and tear?

No. Normal wear and tear cannot be deducted. Allowed deductions include unpaid rent, abandonment, unpaid utilities and unpaid repair or cleaning the tenant agreed to pay.

What happens to the tenant's deposit if I sell the rental?

It must be given to the new owner or returned to the tenant after lawful deductions. The rule covers sale, assignment, death and receivership.

How quickly must a landlord start repairs on a dangerous condition?

Within 24 hours of notice for conditions that materially interfere with life, health or safety, such as gas hazards or no working exterior locks.

Can a tenant withhold rent for repairs?

A tenant may deduct repair costs only by following the statute: 10 days of written notice, or 48 hours for health and safety conditions, using a licensed or qualified professional and giving the landlord a chance to fix it first.

Can I end a tenancy because I want to sell?

Yes, through the no-fault route, with at least 90 days of notice on form JDF 99 C. Tenants who have lived there less than a year and certain other groups are not covered by that form.

What is landlord retaliation in Colorado?

Acts such as raising rent, cutting services, ending a lease or threatening eviction because a tenant raised habitability issues or joined a tenants' organization.

Colorado Eviction Notice Rules: Notice Types, Days and Selling the House

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Demand for Compliance (JDF 99 A) is used for late rent or lease violation; time to comply is between 3 and 30 days depending on the rental agreement; must be in tenant's primary language. (Residential Evictions, Colorado Judicial Branch; source)
  • Notice to Terminate Tenancy (JDF 99 B) is for repeated or substantial lease violation or criminal behavior; notice period 1 to 91 days depending on the rental agreement. (Residential Evictions, Colorado Judicial Branch; source)
  • Notice of No-Fault Eviction (JDF 99 C), for demolition/conversion, substantial repairs, landlord use, sale of the home, or no new rental agreement, requires at least 90 days; C.R.S. 38-12-1303 requires cause for eviction. (Residential Evictions, Colorado Judicial Branch; C.R.S. 38-12-1303; source)
  • Eviction (FED) is filed in the county where the property is located; after a judgment, a Writ of Restitution (JDF 109) lets the Sheriff physically remove the tenant; court usually gives tenant 48 hours to leave. (Residential Evictions, Colorado Judicial Branch; source)
Selling in Colorado?
We buy Colorado houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Which Colorado court handles a residential eviction?

Evictions are filed in the state court system, which the Colorado Judicial Branch runs through its self-help pages. According to Wikipedia, Colorado is divided into 23 judicial districts, and each has a district court and a county court with limited jurisdiction. The notices and filings described on this page lead to a case in the county where the rental house sits.

The Judicial Branch's Residential Evictions page groups its material into guides, step-by-step forms, subpoenas, frequently asked questions and more resources. It says the branch has compiled all the forms required for house, apartment or condo evictions in one place. It also points to File Without Payment for people who cannot afford the fee and to the Court Resource Centers.

Colorado has 64 counties, so the clerk you deal with depends on the property's address. A landlord with a house in one county and a home in another may have two cases in two courts.

What can happen if a landlord skips the proper steps?

A landlord who skips the legal process can be sued by the tenant. The Judicial Branch's Unlawful Evictions page says landlords must follow the right process, and if they do not, the tenant can file a lawsuit.

If the tenant wins, two remedies are listed:

  • The court can award the tenant money, called damages.
  • A district court can stop the unlawful eviction while the case is pending, which is called an injunction.

This is the main reason owners who plan to sell a rented house should not change locks, shut off utilities or remove belongings. A sale does not give the owner a shortcut around the court process.

How does the tenant's lawsuit move through the court?

The unlawful eviction forms follow a five step order. The same page lists the filings in sequence, and the answer deadline depends on the court.

StepWhat happensForms or timing listed
1Tenant starts the caseComplaint, JDF 601 cover sheet for district court, Form 1 summons for county court or JDF 600 for district court
2Tenant serves the landlordJDF 98 Affidavit of Service
3Landlord respondsDue within 14 days in county court, 21 days in district court
4Hearing preparationJDF 71 witness list, JDF 72 exhibit list, subpoena forms
5As neededJDF 205 motion to waive the filing fee; restraining order motion in district court

The restraining order motion has no standard form and is part of the district court process only.

Why does the notice type matter before a sale?

The notice you serve sets the clock for everything after it. This page's sections above describe the notice types Colorado uses and how many days each requires. Pick the one that matches the reason you are ending the tenancy, because a wrong or late notice means starting over.

An owner who wants to sell has a few paths:

  • Serve the notice that fits the situation, then sell after the tenant leaves.
  • Sell the house with the tenant still in it, to a buyer who agrees to take it that way.
  • Agree on a move-out date with the tenant in writing.
  • Sell for cash as-is and let the buyer handle the occupancy question.

Each path has a cost in time, and a buyer who needs a vacant house has to wait for the tenant to leave. A buyer who accepts an occupied house does not.

Do rented Colorado houses pay income tax when sold?

A rental house that was never your residence does not qualify for the home sale exclusion. IRS Topic 701 grants up to $250,000 of exclusion, or $500,000 on a joint return, only for a main home that passes the ownership and use tests, which each require 24 months in the five years before the sale.

Colorado follows the federal figure. The Department of Revenue's nonresident guidance says income from real property located in Colorado, including capital gains, is Colorado source income. An out of state landlord who sells a Colorado rental will usually see the closing agent withhold the lesser of 2 percent of the sale price or the net proceeds, claimable on a Colorado return.

If you ever lived in the house, the exclusion may still apply in part. Ask a tax professional before you decide.

What does Colorado weather and geography mean for a rented house?

A rented house takes the same weather as any other. Wikipedia notes that the eastern Plains are subject to some of the biggest hail storms in North America, and that severe hail hit Denver on July 11, 1990 and May 8, 2017. It also lists large wildfires, including the Marshall Fire of December 30, 2021, described as the most destructive in the state by property loss.

If a tenant dispute turns on repairs, keep photos, invoices and insurance claims in one folder.

  • Roof and gutter condition after hail seasons.
  • Defensible space around the house in wildfire areas.
  • Records of what the tenant reported and when.

How do Colorado regions change an eviction and sale?

Where the house sits changes who your buyers are and how quickly they appear. Wikipedia describes Colorado as a state of 6,012,561 people in 2025, with Denver as the capital and largest city and El Paso as the largest county. The Front Range Urban Corridor holds the main metro areas, including Denver, Colorado Springs, Pueblo and Greeley. On the Western Slope, the larger population centers are Grand Junction, Durango and Montrose.

Roughly half the state is flat and rolling land east of the Rockies, with precipitation of 15 to 25 inches a year. The rest is mountain and desert country. A rented house in a Front Range suburb and one in a small mountain town may share the same notice rules but face very different buyer pools.

What reporting do you owe after selling a rental house?

Expect paperwork even when the gain is small. Under IRS Topic 701, if you receive a Form 1099-S, you must report the sale even when the gain is excludable, and you must report it when you cannot exclude all of the gain. The IRS points to Schedule D and Form 8949 for reporting.

Colorado adds its own return. According to the Department of Revenue, nonresidents with Colorado source income must file a Colorado return when they must file a federal return or owe Colorado tax. Withholding at closing is claimed on the line for form DR 1079, not the W-2 or 1099 line, and a refund is allowed if it exceeds the tax owed.

What do landlords selling a house in Colorado usually run into?

The common problems are a tenant who stops paying, a lease that runs past the planned sale date and a house that needs work. Each one slows a standard listing, because lenders and buyers want vacant, move-in ready homes.

A cash sale as-is removes several of those steps. We buy houses in Colorado in their current condition, including rentals with tenants, and we can talk through the notice timeline before you commit. This page is general information and not legal advice, so confirm forms and deadlines with the court or a licensed attorney.

More questions about Colorado Eviction Notice Rules

Can a Colorado tenant sue a landlord for an unlawful eviction?

Yes. The Colorado Judicial Branch says that if a landlord does not follow the right process, the tenant can file a lawsuit and may be awarded damages.

How long does a landlord have to answer a tenant's unlawful eviction case?

The response is due within 14 days in county court and within 21 days in district court, according to the Judicial Branch's forms page.

Where do I find Colorado eviction forms?

The Colorado Judicial Branch has compiled the forms for house, apartment and condo evictions on its Residential Evictions self-help page.

Can I sell a house with a tenant in it in Colorado?

Yes, you can sell it, but the tenancy continues until it is lawfully ended. A buyer who will take it occupied, or a cash buyer, is usually the fastest route.

Is the gain on a rental house sale taxable in Colorado?

It can be. A house you never lived in does not meet the federal use test, and Colorado treats gain from Colorado real property as Colorado source income.
